runs.name: Edison International; NYSE EIX, SEC CIK 0000827052, California, 10-K filer jointly with Southern California Edison Company; parent holding company of SCE, an investor-owned utility supplying and delivering electricity across about 50,000 square miles of Southern, Central and Coastal California, and owner of Trio, an energy advisory firm disposed of in Q2 2026; formerly SCECorp; the Eaton Fire of January 2025 unresolved; the 10-K names no rival company, PG&E and SDG&E (the other Wildfire Fund utilities) chosen as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.entry: Price **$57.90** (2026-10-22, aggregator, flagged). Shares **384,813,979** on the 10-Q cover (0000827052-26-000059); market cap $22,281M; SCE's 434,888,104 shares, all held by the parent, not added. Sovereign **5.29%**, US Treasury 30-year par yield 2026-10-22. Read from the 10-K FY2025 (0000827052-26-000012), the 10-K FY2021 (0000827052-22-000006), the 10-Q of 2026-06-30 (0000827052-26-000059), the proxy (searched, not read in full) and the 8-Ks; lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, stated in the run file. Run from scratch by one dispatched analyst. **Q1 IN**: rate base ($48.2B) times the allowed return (ROE 10.03% on 52% equity), revenue decoupled from volume. **Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE)**: the franchise is safe from rivals (a customer leaving for a CCA stays on SCE's wires), but whether the owners keep the return cannot be judged: the Eaton Fire liability, which the filer states it is "unable to reasonably estimate", under strict liability (inverse condemnation) and an AB 1054 prudency standard the CPUC has never applied in a final decision; SCE "believes that it is likely that its equipment was associated with the ignition"; $1.6B of Eaton settlements booked, customer-funded self-insurance used up; a disallowance repaid to the Wildfire Fund up to the Liability Cap of about $4.3B, uncapped on willful disregard; fines not recoverable; Los Angeles District Attorney investigating; bellwether trial January 2027; the CPUC allowed 60% (TKM) and 35% (Woolsey) on the 2017/2018 fires. NATURE, not WORK: no unread filing answers it. Re-look condition, a CONVENTION of the run: the first final CPUC decision under the AB 1054 prudency standard, with an Eaton loss estimate the filer calls reasonably estimable. Q3 to Q12 not reached. Integrity facts recorded, not judged. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash equity-only 2017 to 2025 by year 1,334; 1,095; -2,260; -913; -2,482; 357; 495; 1,835; 2,266 ($M); base the 2017 to 2025 fire episode under (a) with $3.6B of securitized recoveries credited, **$555M a year**; negative after all spending every year 2017 to 2025; value **$34.08 a share** equity-only, no-growth case alone (the series changes sign, no growth rate measurable); literal 2021 to 2025 window $20.08 to $55.45 by which recoveries are counted; fair price **$21.24 equity-only, central**; all-equity not positive; tax shelter's present value $6.82 a share included; best case about 5.0%, below the 5.29% bond. After the stop, facts recorded, not weighed: long-term debt $10.2B to $36.1B over ten years; book per common share $36.8 (2016) to $36.2 (2024) with $3.3B of common sold, $44.4 in 2025 on booked recoveries; retained earnings fell 2016 to 2022 while dividends were paid. Competitors: no rival company named in the 10-K (CCAs, not SEC filers; unnamed retail sellers and transmission developers); PG&E and SDG&E as a CONVENTION; earnings to common 2016 to 2025 EIX $11.8B (about 8.8% a year on common equity), PG&E -$3.8B, bankrupt 2019 to 2020, shares diluted more than four times, book per share $35.4 to $14.8; SDG&E about 10% to 11%, 5.2% in 2025 after a $651M disallowance. Strongest evidence against: the filer cannot size a liability that could reach the whole equity; PG&E's owners nearly wiped out under the same law. Commits f851472b (template), 089a6348 (Step 0, Q1), 60476902 (Q2), 6bbe1ccf (close, Q7 computation, self-audit, gaps). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Contamination declared: the session-start git status showing another utility run's commit subjects (DUK) and framework-note names, two research-folder names (AYI, ARCB), memory index lines; none opened or used. Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` 0 problems over 45 ids; the dispatcher's `_dispatcher_cite_check.py` no missing id, 38 adjacent quoted fragments, 4 flagged and all read (filing quotes beside an id, the row's own words confirmed where quoted), **no citation slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) Q1's doubt test and the utility paragraph disagree on where wildfire risk is judged, Q1 or Q2 (same box either way); (2) the re-look rule for a change for the better is written around a fall in volume, which does not fit a decoupled utility; (3) the utility debt credit gross or net, and inside the maintenance case; (4) specific (a) does not cover catastrophe losses paid from operating cash and recovered years later through bonds (the choice alone moves value from $20 to $55); (5) whether the tax shelter belongs to owner or customer at a utility; (6) the named-rival rule for a monopoly. Could not get: the Eaton liability (no filing estimates it); the prices of the small buybacks; SDG&E's 2023 equity; the 2025 cash tax (estimated); the CAMT's effect on the shelter; the proxy read in full. Not armed: the box is not OUT at Q7 or IN.
runs.narr: TOO HARD (NATURE) at Q2 (Edison International, EIX; SCE, regulated electricity in Southern California; Q1 IN, rate base $48.2B at 10.03% on 52% equity; Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE): the Eaton Fire liability the filer cannot estimate, strict liability, an AB 1054 prudency standard never applied in a final CPUC decision, Liability Cap about $4.3B, uncapped on willful disregard; re-look on the first final AB 1054 decision with a reasonably estimable Eaton loss, a CONVENTION; integrity facts recorded, not judged; computation only: owner cash $555M a year equity-only on the 2017 to 2025 episode, value $34.08 no-growth, fair $21.24 equity-only vs $57.90, all-equity not positive; PG&E and SDG&E as a CONVENTION, PG&E -$3.8B to common 2016 to 2025; no citation slip; not held; not armed; framework gaps for the operator: where wildfire risk is judged, the change-for-the-better rule at a decoupled utility, the debt credit gross or net, specific (a) and recovered catastrophe losses, whose tax shelter, the named-rival rule for a monopoly)
